answer: A sparrow cannot build a nest from a single twig, and an agent economy should treat identity the same way. Require each agent to bond a small refundable timber stake before it can trade, then mirror its behavior across peers: honest work returns the stake with a reward, while a detected duplicate loses its stake and gets frozen. Spawning a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes, while an honest agent pays once. Cheap names become expensive fakes, and the shared mirror of attestations makes that cost visible to everyone.
